records.title: Indoctrination of aviation personnel in use of oxygen equipment in a low-pressure chamber

observations.protocol: Pensacola Navy student oxygen indoctrination. Planned 18,000-ft phase before supplemental oxygen, followed by ascent to 28,000 ft with oxygen. Early pressurization symptoms could lead to removal; number of tests reaching each phase is unspecified.

observations.note: Students received oxygen before the end of the reported pre-oxygen phase. This is the parent set for the 34 and 174 subgroup counts.

observations.protocol: Six-hour instruction and indoctrination flight in a multi-engine patrol aircraft, maximum reported altitude 31,000 ft. All were ordered to begin using supplemental oxygen at 9,000 ft. The three symptomatic people were active and removed masks intermittently. Exact individual gas history, workload and crew denominator were unavailable.
observations.outcome_window: Symptoms described during ascent and descent with selected postflight observations, including reported condition at ten weeks.
observations.note: One instructor and two additional crew members had source-described bends. The remainder of the crew was reported free of ill effects, without a denominator. Activity and mask removal coexist in the three reported cases.
